propositions.question: Which Cursor artifact and surface does this record identify?
propositions.answer: The publisher download archive names exact desktop client 3.14 and versioned platform endpoints. No package, digest, source revision or installed runtime was captured.
propositions.whyItMatters: A proprietary client version can be exact while its invoked artifact and hosted backend remain unresolved.

propositions.question: What can the publisher-documented foreground Agent surface do?
propositions.status: Mode- and tool-dependent local IDE authority
propositions.answer: Rolling documentation describes Agent, Ask, Manual and Custom modes plus search, read, edit, delete, terminal, web and MCP tools. Their effective availability is unknown.
propositions.whyItMatters: The surface name alone does not establish the selected mode or enabled tools.

propositions.question: How can terminal, MCP and Fetch actions proceed?
propositions.status: Manual, allowlisted, sandboxed and classifier-reviewed paths remain separate
propositions.answer: Publisher sources describe manual MCP approval, Auto-run and Auto-review paths involving allowlists, sandboxing, a classifier and possible user approval. No effective path was inspected.
propositions.whyItMatters: Different settings can materially change consequential-action authority under the same client identity.

propositions.question: Which client, target, mode and model configuration was active?
propositions.answer: Platform, foreground target, interaction mode, tool set, MCP state, run mode, Auto-review path, model selection and Privacy Mode remain unresolved alternatives.
propositions.whyItMatters: Client version 3.14 is not a complete runtime or model identity.

propositions.question: Where can Agent requests and code data go?
propositions.status: Cursor backend plus configuration-dependent providers and privacy terms
propositions.answer: Current publisher pages say AI requests, including bring-your-own-key requests, traverse Cursor's backend; Privacy Mode changes training and provider-retention commitments with stated exceptions.
propositions.whyItMatters: A local foreground client still depends on rolling hosted services and configuration-specific data terms.
